title: Deadline-aware microburst packer for streaming chat to reduce tail latency and GPU memory churn
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Streaming chat workloads show microbursts of short requests interleaved with longer generations. Our current continuous batcher either (a) dispatches immediately and pays heavy tail latency during high contention, or (b) waits too long to coalesce and harms P50. Additionally, KV cache allocation and slab reserves jitter under bursty arrivals, causing opportunistic GPU OOMs and frequent small evictions that hurt throughput.

Goal: Implement a deadline-aware microburst packing heuristic that: (1) respects per-request streaming latency budgets, (2) opportunistically coalesces short windows of arrivals into low-jitter microbatches, (3) stabilizes KV slab reservations and eviction patterns to reduce memory churn, and (4) preserves fairness across sessions/tenants. Target SLO: P95 generation token latency <= 160ms for short-turn chat completions under 95th-percentile load, and reduce small-eviction frequency by >= 40% on stress traces.

Approach summary:
- Introduce soft-deadlines per incoming chunk derived from client-declared latency preference (fast/standard) and historical session pacing.
- Maintain a short lookahead buffer (configurable 2-15ms) and a microburst aggregator that holds requests until either the soft-deadline expires or the microbatch reaches a size heuristic.
- Use a deadline-weighted packing score to rank coalescing candidates: score = alpha*(remaining_deadline_ms) + beta*(predicted_token_length) + gamma*(session_priority). Lower score -> higher packing priority.
- For KV cache: implement slot pre-reservation for requests expected to touch KV (chat continuations) and a slab smoothing policy that increments reserves in small deltas instead of immediate full expansion. This reduces transient OOMs and evictions.
- GPU memory policy: maintain a headroom watermark per GPU (configurable, default 12%) and evaluate speculative quantized execution (int8 fallback) when headroom is low and request can tolerate small quality delta.
- Fairness: ensure that long-running, greedy sessions cannot starve microburst aggregation by capping per-session tokens-in-flight used for batch decisioning.

Why unique: This ticket focuses on deadline-first packing for streaming chat (not purely latency-first or throughput-first) and couples the batch formation heuristic with KV reservation smoothing and GPU headroom-aware fallbacks — a coordinated cross-layer strategy rather than independent knobs.

Risks/Unknowns:
- Client-declared latency preferences may be missing or abused; need conservative defaults and rate limits.
- Predicted token-length model needs training/tuning on production traces to avoid mispack.
- Interaction with distributed routing: when routing across capacity tiers we must preserve deadlines or risk inter-region tail spikes.

Success metrics (see acceptance_criteria): P95/P99 latency, small-eviction frequency, GPU OOM incidence, throughput impact.
acceptance_criteria: P95 generation token latency for short completions (<= 8 tokens) under 95th-percentile arrival trace <= 160ms
Small-eviction events (slab < 4MB triggers) reduced by >= 40% on replay of 2026-02 production bursts
No increase in overall cost-per-token > 5% compared to baseline simulated load
Feature gated and can be rolled back at runtime; config flags for lookahead_ms and headroom_pct
Integration tests that simulate interleaved microbursts and long sessions with assertions on batch sizes and reservation deltas
implementation_notes:
High-level algorithm (prototype):
1) On chunk arrival, attach a computed soft_deadline_ms = client_latency_pref_ms * deadline_scale(session_history).
2) Insert into microburst_buffer indexed by affinity_key (model + tenant + session_shard).
3) Periodically (every scheduler_tick_ms = 1ms) consider buffer: compute packing_score for candidate set and attempt to form microbatch up to gpu_token_budget or until any candidate's soft_deadline <= tick_slack_ms.
4) Before dispatch, call kv_pre_reserve(batch) which calculates incremental slab growth: delta = min(max_delta_bytes, predicted_kv_bytes - current_reserve). Apply in small increments; if global_mem_headroom < headroom_pct, mark requests with speculative_quantize=true.
5) Dispatch: update per-session tokens-in-flight counters and start per-request deadline timers; collect runtime telemetry for observed latency and kv_eviction events.

Notes on parameters to tune: lookahead_ms ∈ [2,15], alpha/beta/gamma weight grid search, headroom_pct default 12%, max_delta_bytes default 8MB.

Prototype artifacts: initial simulator (python) generates synthetic traces of short microbursts + long sessions. Use replay harness to drive dedicated dev cluster with small-scale GPUs to validate eviction frequency changes.
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Triage and spec by Maya. Decided to scope initial rollout to hosted API paths for streaming chat only (no private runtime yet).

2026-03-11: Simulator prototype finished (python harness). Ran 5k trace replays; microburst packing reduced average batch creation events by ~28% in synthetic load. Logged simulator code in /confluence/runtime/2026/deadline-microburst/simulator and added sample traces to drive-tests bucket.

2026-03-12: Implemented microburst_buffer and packing_score in batcher-v2 branch. Initial CI unit tests green. Hooked kv_pre_reserve stub; added feature flag runtime.deadline_microburst = false by default.

2026-03-13: Benchmarked on dev-gpu-4 (A10x4) with replay trace; observed P95 drop for short completions from 220ms -> 150ms, small-eviction delta -36% (below target but promising). Identified jitter in slab growth under heavy concurrent demands.
2026-03-14: Updated slab smoothing to use additive-increase cap and introduced per-tenant reserve ceiling to avoid noisy neighbor expansion. Preparing PR for internal review (see prs).
review_feedback: PM (Rosa Alvarez): prefer conservative defaults for lookahead_ms; user-facing latency settings must be exposed in Console as 'streaming_preference'
SRE (Liam O'Connor): add observability for kv_pre_reserve events and GPU headroom transitions; surface alerts when speculative_quantize > 10%
Design (Priya Nair): when clients fall back to speculative_quantize, we need a UI signal in console and include quality-regression metric in Optimize dashboards
Eng (Kenji Matsuda): ensure packer respects existing priority-aware allocator to avoid regressions for enterprise reserved capacity customers; suggested integration test with Dedicated pool routing
